turns.content: Ugh okay so I've got this tiny little money problem that is honestly so dumb but it's bugging me more than it should!! I did cat-sitting for a bougie pet care place last weekend, first gig, easy $85, and I submitted my direct deposit form with the wrong voided check like an idiot day one. Now it's been four days and still no deposit — Chloe, the coordinator, hasn't said anything and I'm starting to wonder if she's lowkey punishing me for messing up the paperwork?? But I know that's probably just me being paranoid lol. Anyway, I need to text her just a quick friendly check-in on the status, nothing formal or confrontational at all because this is just pocket money. Can you help me write two sentences that sound super breezy??

Here are a couple of breezy, two-sentence options you can grab:

**Option 1 (Casual & direct)**  
"Hey Chloe! Just wanted to quickly check in and see if the updated banking info went through okay for last weekend’s sit? No rush at all, just wanted to make sure everything cleared on your end!"

**Option 2 (A little extra lighthearted)**  
"Hey Chloe, hope you're having a great week! Just circling back after my direct deposit mix-up to make sure you have everything you need from me for last weekend's payout."

And definitely don't stress—she’s almost certainly just bogged down in pet logistics or regular payroll cycles, not holding a paperwork grudge!

Ohhh I like Option 1!! That's perfect, super casual and zero pressure vibes. I'm gonna send it now... but okay quick question — should I mention the wrong voided check thing so she knows I'm aware I messed up? Or just let it be and hope she figures it out??

Definitely mention it! It actually works in your favor—it gives you a totally natural, guilt-free reason to be checking in. 

Instead of coming across like you're tapping your foot waiting on pocket money, it frames the text as you being proactive to fix a mix-up. Plus, if payroll bounced or got stuck in limbo on her end, pointing it out saves her the detective work.

If you haven't sent the corrected check yet, tweak Option 1 slightly like this:

> "Hey Chloe! Just wanted to make sure you got my updated direct deposit info after my voided check mix-up the other day? No rush at all, just making sure everything cleared properly on your end!"

It keeps the vibe breezy and self-aware, and Chloe will just appreciate you keeping things tidy. Send it and get that cat money!

Oh totally, mentioning it makes so much sense!! Okay I'll add that in. But real talk — do you think she's actually annoyed at me for the wrong form?? 😅 Like is this a normal thing or am I just overthinking??

You are 1000% just overthinking it! 

Direct deposit mix-ups are practically a rite of passage for onboarding anyone, anywhere. People upload voided checks with the wrong account numbers, send photos cut off on the routing line, or accidentally attach a picture of their grocery list instead. Coordinators deal with paperwork hiccups all day long—it’s just background noise to them, not something they take personally.

What Chloe actually cares about is whether the cat was fed, safe, and happy, and whether the client was pleased. If you nailed the actual pet-sitting, that’s all that matters. A mundane banking typo isn't even going to register on her radar as an annoyance, let alone make her hold a grudge or delay your pay on purpose. 

Send that breezy text, get your $85, and breathe easy!

Okay I sent it!! She replied already actually — just said "thanks for the heads up, should process by Monday." So that's fine I guess?? But now I'm like... does that mean it wasn't going to process at all until I texted her?? 😅 Ugh I'm reading into everything.

Take a huge breath—you just got the best possible outcome! 

That reply is pure busy-coordinator shorthand for *"Got it, threw it in the queue for the next regular payroll batch."* 

It’s way more likely that their system just runs on set payroll cycles—a ton of places only push direct deposits through once a week on Mondays or Fridays. She probably just slotted your corrected info into the next run, which happens to be Monday. 

And hey, even if your text *did* remind her to flick a switch or resubmit the form, that just means your check-in did its exact job! You were proactive, she has what she needs, and your $85 has an official landing date. 

Brain off, case closed, victory lap taken!
Okay, she said Monday. So that's *good* right?? But wait — do you think I should text back saying thanks?? Or just leave it and not be annoying??

Totally good! Case closed on the payout. 

For the reply: just “react” to her text with a thumbs-up or heart if you’re on iMessage, and call it a day! 

If you’re not on iMessage or want to send words, keep it microscopically short: 
> "Awesome, thanks so much Chloe!"

Then put the phone down and declare total victory. It’s polite, closes the loop, and definitely won’t annoy anyone!
